Published online:
September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
Global (US, Japan, Germany, UK, France, Australia); primary focus on US

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
Global sovereign bond yields are surging driven by rising real (inflation-adjusted) yields, not just inflation expectations. Fed Chair Warsh signaled at Jackson Hole that US financial conditions remain loose and policy is not meaningfully restrictive, pushing Fed futures to price ~70% probability of a September hike and two full hikes by March 2027. The structural driver is a global upward revision of the neutral rate ("R-star"), fueled by the AI capital expenditure boom lifting corporate borrowing, investment demand, and growth. With real Fed policy rates near zero and the AI buildout expanding globally, multiple major central banks face the same challenge: locating a neutral rate that has likely shifted materially higher.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — Core of the article is US Treasury yields, Fed Chair Warsh's policy stance, Fed futures pricing, real US rates, and neutral rate reassessment.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 95 (strongly YES)
Probability of increase: ~70% for September hike; two hikes fully priced by March 2027

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (effectively NO)
Probability of holding: ~30% for September (implied residual from hike probability)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO — cuts are explicitly absent; futures strip shows policy rate never falling below 4% through 2028)
Probability of decrease: <5%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 85 (Strongly hawkish — Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks directly challenged the "restrictive" narrative, financial conditions described as loose, real rates near zero, Fed futures rapidly repriced toward near-term hikes, and the structural neutral rate revision points to a durably higher rate environment ahead)
